title: を — marks the direct object
summary: を marks the thing that a verb acts on, the direct object: ‘do something to ～’. It follows a noun and comes before a verb. It is written を but pronounced ‘o’.

patterns.gloss: noun + を + transitive verb (りんごを食べる)

body.p: The word before を is the thing that receives the action: りんごを食べます (eat an apple), 新聞を読みます (read a newspaper), 手紙を書きます (write a letter). The word order is object + を + verb.
を is pronounced ‘o’, the same as お. Today it is used almost only as this particle, so remember it as the object marker.
A time word such as 毎朝 does not take を; it just sits near the start of the sentence. Also, を is used with verbs that take an object. Verbs like 行く and 来る take に or へ for their destination instead.

examples.note: りんご receives the action 食べる.

examples.ja: 毎朝（まいあさ）、新聞（しんぶん）を読（よ）みます。
examples.tr: I read the newspaper every morning.

examples.ja: 手紙（てがみ）を書（か）きます。

pitfalls: を is pronounced ‘o’, not ‘wo’, but must be written as を, not お.
Don't use を for destinations: 学校へ行きます, not 学校を行きます.
